summary: Runs an NVIDIA Flow smoke/fire fluid simulation with emitter, simulation, combustion, allocation, and debug rendering controls.

key_params.name: camera
key_params.note: Perspective Camera COMP used to view the simulation.

key_params.name: emitters
key_params.note: NVIDIA Flow Emitter COMPs included in the simulation.

key_params.name: simposition
key_params.note: World-space center of the simulation volume.

key_params.name: simsize
key_params.note: World-space size of the simulation volume and block scale.

key_params.name: memusage
key_params.note: Relative fraction of simulation blocks allocated for the volume.

key_params.name: showblocks
key_params.note: Display simulation blocks and volume edges for debugging.

key_params.name: shadowresolution
key_params.note: Resolution of the volume shadow map texture.

common_gotchas: Official docs mark NVIDIA Flow TOP as Windows-only and NVIDIA-GPU-only.
The camera must use perspective projection.
Smaller simulation blocks increase accuracy but require more GPU work.
High memusage can cause extremely high memory usage.
MacCormack blend controls can sharpen the result but may introduce artifacts.
key_concepts: Runs and renders a volumetric NVIDIA Flow fire, smoke, and burning-gas simulation.
Requires one or more NVIDIA Flow Emitter COMPs and a perspective Camera COMP.
Simulation position and size define the bounded volume where gas can exist.
Memory allocation, debug block views, and volume-shadow controls are central to performance tuning.
